 "Briefed Multiple Times"... Collusion Between Politics and Business Leaves National Security Vulnerable
 Hong Yeongjae 
 Seoul 
 Published 
 2026.11.12 06:37 
 View 
 View Count 
 PIP 닫기 
 〈Anchor〉 
 Allegations that U.S. President Donald Trump overlooked the potential leakage of classified information or technology through Jensen Huang even after receiving briefings are becoming a major issue in U.S. politics. The U.S. opposition party is criticizing that President Trump, who has spearheaded export controls against China, has instead put the U.S. at risk of security threats. 
 Reporter Hong Yeongjae has the story. 
 〈Reporter〉 
 The New York Times reported that last May, aboard Air Force One en route to China for the U.S.-China summit, President Trump received a direct briefing from Secretary of State Marco Rubio regarding allegations that Jensen Huang was linked to Chinese espionage. 
 Despite this, President Trump hurriedly had Jensen Huang board the plane in Alaska—someone who was not originally on the itinerary for the visit to China—and traveled with him to Beijing. 
 [Donald Trump / U.S. President : (Were you aware at the time of your visit to China in May of this year of allegations linking Jensen Huang to Chinese espionage?) No. I didn't hear about that at the time.] 
 President Trump reportedly took no particular action despite receiving briefings on the related suspicions at least twice over a span of 7 months. 
 Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick was also reported to have circulated a memo regarding Jensen Huang written by Secretary Rubio, yet last May, the U.S. Department of Commerce approved 10 Chinese companies to purchase Nvidia H200 chips. 
 Within the U.S., suspicions are being raised that collusion between Jensen Huang and the Trump administration—and furthermore, Chinese espionage operations attempting to exploit this—may have been at play. 
 [Jensen Huang / Nvidia CEO (October of last year) : Whether it's through negotiations by President Trump, or because China wants U.S. companies to return to China, if we can re-enter the Chinese market, it will be a huge boon for us.] 
 The controversy is spreading to other big tech companies as well. 
 Big tech chiefs who attended President Trump's inauguration in flocks in January of last year donated a total of $44.6 million—about 59.5 billion won—just in campaign funds that day. In return, the Trump administration provided various benefits to big tech firms, including Nvidia, such as easing export controls and simplifying permit processes. This is why criticism is emerging that such collusion between politics and business is even threatening national security. 
 [Chris Coons / U.S. Senator : Ordinary Americans watching President Trump's inauguration must have thought, 'What kind of corruption is actually going on here?'.] 
 As the U.S. Democratic Party has signaled a sweeping investigation into suspicions of collusion between the Trump administration and big tech companies, the fallout is expected to continue to grow.
